claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to gather some information about you and your circumstances.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you're enquiring about for Child Benefit?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to check if I'm eligible for Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a few questions to assess eligibility for Alex.

**Does Alex live with you?** Or does he live with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?** For example, is he attending school, college, or an approved training programme?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for clarifying that.

Let me ask one more important question to ensure I have the full picture:

**Is Alex in any kind of care arrangement, such as being in local authority care, or is he receiving any other form of state support that might affect his eligibility?** Or is he simply living at home with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's just living at home with me. He's not in any kind of care or receiving any state support.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me check the eligibility rules to make sure I have the correct understanding before providing my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide my assessment.

**Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you can normally qualify for Child Benefit if your child is 16 or over **only if they stay in approved education or training**. The rules state: "You'll normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training."

Since Alex is 17 years old and is **not currently in any education or training**, he does not meet the eligibility criteria. While there is a provision that allows you to claim for up to 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you would need to register him in one of those services for this to apply.

If Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service, you may be able to claim for a limited period. I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office to discuss this option if that becomes relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I hope this clarifies your situation. If you have any other questions or if Alex's circumstances change (such as him starting education, training, or registering with a careers service), please feel free to get in touch.
